story.title: The Weight of Yesterday
story.logline: A man discovers he is not living his own life, but a perfectly curated simulation of someone else's best day.
story.theme: The existential terror of manufactured happiness.
story.twist: The protagonist discovers he is the reward being gifted to a grieving customer as an immersive experience.
story.ending: He realizes his entire existence is a product with an expiration date.

scenes.narration: My daughter just turned seven for the fifth time today, and she still hasn't learned to tie her shoes.
scenes.visual_prompt: A 30-year-old man, Elias, with short dark hair in a gray sweater, stands in a bright sunlit kitchen.

scenes.narration: The morning sun hits the table at the exact same angle. I reach for my coffee. It's always lukewarm.
scenes.visual_prompt: Elias, 30, dark hair, gray sweater, reaches for a coffee mug in the same bright kitchen.

scenes.narration: I kiss my wife, Sarah. Her skin is soft, but her eyes never quite focus on mine when I speak.
scenes.visual_prompt: Elias, 30, dark hair, gray sweater, kisses a woman in a kitchen, but she stares blankly at the wall.

scenes.narration: Yesterday, I tried to walk out the front door. I found a solid, unyielding wall of static instead.
scenes.visual_prompt: Elias, 30, dark hair, gray sweater, touches a wall that flickers with digital grain.

scenes.narration: Everything here is a loop. A perfect, polished loop designed to keep me from ever feeling actual, stinging pain.
scenes.visual_prompt: Elias, 30, dark hair, gray sweater, looks at his reflection in a mirror, gripping the edges tightly.

scenes.narration: I found a remote tucked under the floorboards. One button. It labels this world as 'Package 402: Idealized Family'.
scenes.visual_prompt: Elias, 30, dark hair, gray sweater, holds a metallic remote, looking at a small holographic screen.

scenes.narration: I am not a father. I am not a husband. I am an animation meant to soothe a lonely client.
scenes.visual_prompt: Elias, 30, dark hair, gray sweater, stands alone in the kitchen as the room begins to pixelate.

scenes.narration: Beyond the static, I hear a woman weeping. She is the one paying for my every single gentle smile.
scenes.visual_prompt: Elias, 30, dark hair, gray sweater, looks up at the ceiling as audio of sobbing plays loudly.

scenes.narration: The subscription is running low. The colors are washing out. My life is literally flickering out of existence now.
scenes.visual_prompt: Elias, 30, dark hair, gray sweater, watches his hands slowly turn into translucent particles.

scenes.narration: My daughter just turned seven for the last time, and I am finally allowed to stop being a memory.
scenes.visual_prompt: Elias, 30, dark hair, gray sweater, smiles sadly as he vanishes completely into bright white light.

caption.hook: Your happiest memory is just a product.
caption.title: The Weight of Yesterday
caption.caption: Every laugh feels authentic, yet every sunset is scripted for someone else’s comfort. When you're just a prize in a grieving stranger's dream, does your soul actually belong to you? Are you living, or just being consumed?
